modules.module_title: Planning and Cutting on Brass Sheet

pcs.pc_description: Plan a design and carefully cut out a brass sheet.
Design is cut out from a thin brass sheet using tools like a jeweler’s saw.
Ensure that the intricate patterns are accurately replicated onto the stone.

modules.module_title: Tracing the Design on the Base Stone

pcs.pc_description: Place the brass sheet template on the base sandstone.
Trace the design on the stone surface using a fine pencil or marker.
Use chisels, a set-square, and other carving tools, the stone is carved along the traced lines to create recesses or grooves.
Depth and width of the grooves must be carefully controlled to match the thickness of the colored stones that will be inlaid.
Select different color stones to fit into the carved grooves.
Cut the stones into small pieces that match the shapes needed for the design.
Use traditional tools like a diamond-tipped saw or water jet cutter, depending on the hardness and fragility of the sandstone.
Grooves are further refined to ensure the shaped stones fit perfectly.
Apply an adhesive, such as epoxy resin or a stone-specific glue to the grooves, and the cut stones are carefully placed and press into them.
Polish using abrasive materials, such as sandpaper or diamond pads, to smooth out the surface and level the inlay with the base sandstone.
Polish the edges of the inlay work to remove any sharpness and to enhance the visual appeal.
Check for any imperfections, such as gaps between the inlay pieces and the base stone, loose stones, or uneven surfaces.
Correction often by filling gaps or repolishing certain areas.
Ensure the finished product meets the desired standards and quality of the product.

pcs.pc_description: Identify and source high-quality black marble and semi-precious stones as per design specifications.
Inspect and prepare tools such as chisels, grinders, and engraving tools for functionality and precision.
Clean and level the marble surface to ensure proper adherence for inlay work.
Ensure the availability of adhesives and polishing agents suitable for marble inlay.
Interpret the design requirements from sketches, blueprints, or client briefs.
Accurately transfer the design onto the black marble using stencils, tracing, or hand drawing.
Verify alignment, proportions, and dimensions of the design on the marble surface.
Modify the design layout, if necessary, to suit the marble’s surface or client preferences.
Use cutting tools to shape semi-precious stones as per the design’s intricate patterns.
Ensure that cut stones are of the correct size, shape, and smoothness for embedding.
Polish stones to achieve a glossy finish and enhance their visual appeal.
Follow safety protocols while cutting and shaping materials to prevent injuries.
Engrave precise grooves into the black marble surface to match the design outline.
Ensure that the depth and width of engravings allow for a snug fit of inlay pieces.
Apply adhesives evenly to the grooves for securing inlay materials.
Embed each stone into its respective groove, ensuring proper alignment and tight fitting.
Smooth the marble surface and polish the completed inlay to achieve a flawless finish.
Remove excess adhesive and residue to ensure a clean, professional look.
Inspect the final product for defects, alignment, and overall aesthetic appeal.
Package the finished piece carefully to protect it from damage during storage or transport.
